source.title: UNICON: Combating Label Noise Through Uniform Selection and Contrastive Learning
source.authors: Nazmul Karim; Mamshad Nayeem Rizve; Nazanin Rahnavard; Ajmal Saeed Mian; Mubarak Shah

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training accuracy under label noise and reports that UNICON resists memorization, refining the claim's account of noisy-label fitting. Its results do not test completely random labels or unstructured inputs.
record.gate_note: The training-accuracy plot and its accompanying text bear on V4. The paper discusses simpler patterns being learned before noisy labels are memorized as prior work, but does not test that learning order itself.
record.test_reason: Figure 6 and Section 11.4 directly compare noisy-label fitting under standard CE training and UNICON. This tests the training-fit component of V4 using a modified training method, although it does not establish V4's full train/test relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that uniform selection reduces class disparity and contrastive feature learning combats noisy-label memorization, improving clean-sample selection, pseudo-label quality, and performance under high label noise.
record.recipe_differences: UNICON uses class-balanced sample selection, semi-supervised learning, and contrastive learning on partially corrupted labels; it does not apply the original random-label intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy changes with noise rate and training method: standard CE memorizes noisy labels, while UNICON resists later memorization; UNICON accuracy deteriorates as noise increases.
record.problems: The relevant training-accuracy values are figure-only and not numerically recoverable from the text. The experiment uses symmetric corruption rather than completely random labels and does not report the full train/test error relationship required by V4.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant training-accuracy conditions are reported in Figure 6; other performance tables report classification test accuracy for the label-noise method but do not measure the claim's specified fitting behavior.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption levels.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit throughout a clean-to-fully-random corruption sweep, paired with steadily increasing test error toward chance. Figure 6 covers only 50% and 80% noise for UNICON and 50% for standard training.
Whether weight decay, dropout, and augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Direct comparison of real-pattern learning and noisy-label memorization over training. The learning-order premise is cited from Arpit et al., rather than independently established.

record.verdict_notes: The standard CE comparator provides qualitative evidence of memorization, but its ambiguous caption and unavailable curve endpoints prevent a verdict on perfect training fit. The test-accuracy tables are declared omitted in rows_left_out; they do not establish simultaneous perfect training fit. UNICON's result concerns an intentionally noise-resistant training procedure.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged standard architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training-time cost of fitting random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

The results do not show test error rising steadily toward chance alongside training accuracy across a sweep from clean to fully random labels; the figure concerns CIFAR10 at 50% and 80% symmetric noise.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent random-label fitting or whether their removal harms true-label generalization.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels over training.

rows.subject: PreAct ResNet18, standard training
rows.operation_detail: Standard CE-loss training on CIFAR10 with symmetric label noise
rows.note: The text says standard CE training reaches high training accuracy, described as about 50% and complete memorization for this noise setting.
rows.check: The text describes increasing accuracy and complete memorization, but the supplied figure text does not establish zero or near-zero training error. The caption's approximately 50% statement is ambiguous and should not be recorded as the measured endpoint or as evidence of perfect fitting. Exact curve values are unavailable.

rows.subject: PreAct ResNet18, UNICON
rows.operation_detail: UNICON training on CIFAR10 with symmetric label noise
rows.note: The text says training accuracy saturates quickly, indicating resistance to later memorization; exact curve values are not stated.
rows.check: The reported early saturation supports incomplete fitting of the supplied noisy labels. Specify that UNICON selects samples, refines labels, generates pseudo-labels, and adds contrastive learning; its result qualifies the training-method scope and does not establish failure of ordinary CE training to memorize.

rows.subject: PreAct ResNet18, UNICON
rows.operation_detail: UNICON training on CIFAR10 with symmetric label noise
rows.note: The text says training accuracy deteriorates as label noise increases; exact curve values are not stated.
rows.check: Section 11.4 reports reduced training accuracy with higher noise and resistance to memorization. Approximately 20% is an ideal clean-label-only reference, not a reported measured endpoint. Specify UNICON's modified training objective and leave the exact observed value unspecified.

relationships.condition: UNICON on CIFAR10 with 50% and 80% symmetric label noise
relationships.reason: R2 and R3 show incomplete noisy-label fitting under deliberate sample selection, label refinement, and contrastive training; Section 11.4 explicitly reports saturation and resistance to memorization. Perfect fitting therefore depends on the training procedure.
relationships.display_finding: Noisy-label fitting saturated below perfect, with the training procedure resisting memorization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: UNICON on CIFAR10 at 50% and 80% symmetric label noise
reader_labels.reason: UNICON's training accuracy saturates and deteriorates as noise increases rather than continuing to memorize noisy labels (R2, R3); the standard CE comparator does memorize at 50% noise (R1). The study does not establish the version's full test-error pattern.
